(p-104) The Chapter of Yunus (Jonah) is Meccan, and it has one hundred and nine verses.

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Most Merciful.

﴿Alif, Lam, Ra﴾. Ibn Kathir and Nafi', in the transmission of Qalun and of Hafs, pronounced it with emphasis (tafkhim, heavy articulation). Warsh read it between the two pronunciations, and the rest of the readers inclined the alif (imalah), treating the alif of the ra' as if it had originated from a ya'.

﴿These are the verses of the Wise Book﴾. The demonstrative refers to what the chapter, or the Qur'an, contains of verses. By "the Book" is meant one of the two. It is described as "wise" either because it comprises wisdom (hukm), or because it is a wise speech, or because its verses are decisive (muhkam), none of them having been abrogated (naskh, the cancellation of a ruling by a later revelation).

﴿Is it a wonder for mankind﴾. This is an interrogative of denial expressing astonishment. "A wonder" (ʿajaban) is the predicate of kana (was), and its subject is the following clause: ﴿that We revealed﴾. It has also been read in the nominative (ʿajabun), on the basis that the matter is the reverse, or on the basis that kana is complete (tammah), in which case ﴿that We revealed﴾ is a substitute (badal) for ʿajaban. The lam (in lil-nas, "for mankind") indicates that they made it an object of wonder for themselves, directing toward it their denial and their mockery.

﴿to a man from among them﴾, that is, from the ordinary members of their clans, not from one of their great notables. It was said that they used to say that the wonder was that God, exalted is He, had not found a messenger to send to mankind except an orphan of Abu Talib. This was out of the extreme foolishness of their minds, the narrowness of their vision in regard to immediate worldly matters, and their ignorance of the reality of revelation and prophethood. Moreover, he (peace and blessings be upon him) did not fall short of their great men in respect of what they regard as important, except in wealth; and poverty of circumstances is the most helpful thing in this matter. For this reason most of the prophets, peace be upon them, before him were likewise. It was also said that they wondered that he had sent a human being as a messenger, as has been mentioned previously in the chapter of al-An'am (The Cattle).

﴿that warn mankind﴾. The "that" (an) is either explanatory (mufassirah) or the light form (mukhaffafah) of the heavy an, in which case it occupies the position of the object of awhayna (We revealed).

﴿and give good news to those who have faith﴾. He generalized the warning, since it is rare for anyone to be without something from which he ought to be warned; and he restricted the good news to the believers, since the disbelievers have nothing with which they can truly be given good news.

﴿that they will have a firm footing (qadam sidq) with their Lord﴾, that is, a precedence and an exalted rank. It is called a "foot" because precedence is attained through it, just as a blessing is called a "hand" because it is given by the hand. Its attribution to "truthfulness" (sidq) is for the sake of its being established, and it alerts to the fact that they attain it only through truthfulness of speech and intention.

﴿The disbelievers said, "Indeed this﴾, meaning the Book and what the Messenger, peace be upon him, brought.

﴿is clearly a sorcery.﴾ Ibn Kathir and the Kufans read it as "lasahir" (is a sorcerer), on the basis that the reference is to the Messenger (ﷺ). This contains an acknowledgment that they encountered from the Messenger (ﷺ) matters that broke the normal course of things, which were miraculous and left them unable to oppose him. It has also been read: "This is only clear sorcery."

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 3:

﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth﴾, which are the origins of the possible beings (al-mumkinat, things whose existence is contingent). ﴿In six days, then He established Himself upon the Throne, arranging the affair﴾, i.e., He determines the affair of beings in accordance with what His wisdom requires and what His word has preceded, and He prepares their causes by setting them in motion and sends them down from Himself. Tadbir (arrangement, management) is the consideration of the outcomes of matters so that they come out with a praiseworthy end. ﴿There is no intercessor except after His permission﴾: this is an affirmation of His greatness and the might of His majesty, and a refutation of those who claimed that their gods would intercede for them with Allah. It also establishes intercession for whomever He permits. ﴿That is Allah﴾, i.e., (p-105) the one described by those attributes which necessitate divinity (uluhiyyah) and lordship (rububiyyah). ﴿Your Lord﴾, and no other, since none shares with Him in any of that.

﴿So worship Him﴾, make Him one in worship. ﴿Will you not then remember?﴾ That is, will you not reflect even a little, so that it would alert you that He is the one deserving of lordship and worship, not what you worship.

To Him is your return, all of you, by death or by resurrection, not to any other. So prepare yourselves for meeting Him. ﴿The promise of God﴾ is an emphatic verbal noun (*masdar mu'akkid*, a verbal noun that confirms its own sense), because His saying ﴿To Him is your return﴾ is a promise from God. ﴿Truly﴾ is another emphatic verbal noun, which confirms something other than itself, namely what is indicated by ﴿the promise of God﴾. ﴿Indeed He originates creation, then repeats it﴾ after its beginning and its annihilation. ﴿That He may recompense those who believed and did righteous deeds with justice﴾: that is, with His justice, or with their own justness and their upholding of justice in their affairs, or with their faith, since it is the upright justice, just as polytheism is great injustice. This last is the most suitable reading, for it corresponds to His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieved, for them is a drink of boiling water and a painful punishment because of what they used to disbelieve.﴾ Its meaning is: that He may recompense those who disbelieved with a drink of boiling water ﴿and a painful punishment﴾ because of their disbelief. But He altered the arrangement, to emphasise that they deserve punishment, and to alert that the purpose in itself of origination and repetition is reward, while punishment occurs incidentally. He, exalted is He, undertakes the reward of the believers with what befits His kindness and generosity, and for this reason He did not specify it. As for the punishment of the disbelievers, it is as though it were a disease that the evil of their beliefs and the ill of their deeds brought upon them. The verse serves as a justification for His saying: ﴿To Him is your return, all of you﴾, for since the purpose of origination and repetition is God's recompensing the responsible persons (*mukallafin*, those obligated by the law) for their deeds, the return of all of them to Him is inevitable. This is supported by the reading of whoever read *(annahu yabda'u)* with a fatha on the *alif* of *anna*, meaning "because He originates." It is also permissible that it be in the accusative or the nominative case, governed by what governs ﴿the promise of God﴾ or by what governs ﴿truly﴾.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 5–6:

﴿He it is who made the sun a radiance﴾, meaning possessing radiance (dhāt ḍiyāʾ). Ḍiyāʾ is either a verbal noun (maṣdar, the infinitive) like qiyām, or the plural of ḍawʾ, like siyāṭ and sawṭ. The yāʾ in it is changed from a wāw.

Ibn Kathir, according to the transmission of Qunbul, read it here, in al-Anbiyaʾ and in al-Qasas as ﴿ḍiʾāʾ﴾ with two hamzas, by way of metathesis (qalb), by moving the lām before the ʿayn. ﴿And the moon a light﴾, meaning possessing light (dhū nūr), or it was called nūr for emphasis. It is more general than ḍawʾ, as you have learned. It has been said: what has radiance in itself is ḍawʾ, and what has it by way of an accident is nūr. By this, God, glorified and exalted be He, has indicated that He created the sun luminous in its essence and the moon luminous by way of its facing the sun and acquiring light from it.

﴿And He determined for it stations﴾. The pronoun refers to each of the two, meaning He determined the course of each of them into stations. Or it refers to the moon alone, meaning He determined it as having stations. The moon is singled out for mention because of the speed of its course, the visibility of its stations, and because the rulings of the Sharia are linked to it. For this reason He gave the reason for it in His words: ﴿so that you may know the number of years and the reckoning﴾, meaning the reckoning of times by months and days in your dealings and transactions.

﴿God did not create that except with truth﴾, meaning except while bound to the truth, taking into account in it the requirement of perfect wisdom.

﴿He details the signs for a people who know﴾, for they are the ones who benefit from reflecting upon them. Ibn Kathir, the two Basrans and Hafs read (yufaṣṣilu) with a yāʾ.

﴿Surely in the alternation of the night and the day, and in what God has created in the heavens and the earth﴾, of kinds of beings, ﴿are signs﴾ indicating the existence of the Creator, His oneness, and the perfection of His knowledge and power, ﴿for a people who are mindful﴾ of the consequences, for this leads them to contemplation and reflection.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (*Anwar al-Tanzil*) on surah 10, verses 7–8:

(p-106)﴿Indeed, those who do not hope for Our meeting﴾ do not expect it, because they deny the resurrection (*al-ba'th*) and are absorbed in sensible things, heedless of what lies beyond them. ﴿And are content with the life of this world﴾ instead of the Hereafter, due to their heedlessness of it. ﴿And are at rest in it﴾ and settle themselves in it, limiting their aspirations to its pleasures and adornments. Or it means they settle in it in the manner of one who is never disturbed from it. ﴿And those who are heedless of Our signs﴾ do not reflect upon them, being immersed in what contradicts them. The conjunction (*al-'atf*) is either because the two descriptions differ, and to draw attention to the threat being directed at combining complete heedlessness of the signs with immersion in desires, such that the Hereafter does not occur to their minds at all; or because the two groups differ. The first group refers to those who deny the resurrection and see nothing but the life of this world, and the second refers to those whom the love of what is immediate (*al-'ajil*) has diverted from contemplating what is deferred (*al-ajil*) and preparing for it.

﴿Those—their refuge is the Fire, because of what they used to earn﴾ because of what they persisted in and trained themselves in, of sins.

**Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 9–10:**

﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, their Lord will guide them by their faith.﴾ *Bi-sabab* (because of) their faith, He guides them to a path that leads to Paradise. Or, He guides them to the realization of the realities (*haqa'iq*), as the Prophet (ﷺ) said, peace and blessings be upon him: "Whoever acts upon what he knows, Allah will bequeath to him the knowledge of what he did not know."

Or, He guides them to what they desire in Paradise. The implied sense (*mafhum al-tartib*, the implied meaning of sequence) indicates that the cause of guidance is faith and righteous deeds. However, the explicit statement (*mantuq*), ﴿by their faith﴾, indicates that faith alone is the independent cause, and that righteous deeds are like a completion and a companion to it.

﴿Rivers flow beneath them﴾: this is a resumptive sentence (*isti'naf*), or a second predicate (*khabar thani*), or a circumstantial clause (*hal*) from the pronoun in the accusative position according to the latter meaning. His saying, ﴿in the Gardens of Bliss﴾, is a predicate or another circumstantial clause from it, or from the rivers, or it is related to ﴿flow﴾ or to ﴿guide﴾.

﴿Their call therein﴾, i.e., their supplication. ﴿Glory be to You, O Allah﴾: meaning, "O Allah, we glorify You with glorification." ﴿And their greeting﴾: that with which some of them greet one another, or the greeting of the angels to them. ﴿Therein, peace; and the end of their call﴾, i.e., the end of their supplication, ﴿is: "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ The *an* here is the lightened form (*al-mukhaffafah*) of the heavy form (*al-thaqilah*), and it has been read in that form. The word *al-hamd* (praise) has also been read in the accusative.

The phrase "*an*" is the light form, meaning that they say this. Perhaps the meaning is that when they enter Paradise and witness the greatness and majesty of Allah, they glorify Him and describe Him with attributes of majesty. Then the angels greet them with safety from calamities and success with various kinds of honors, or Allah, exalted is He, is praised by them, and they extol Him with attributes of generosity.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 11:

﴿And if Allah were to hasten for mankind the evil, as they seek to hasten the good﴾: "and if He were to hasten it for them" (i.e., He would speed it toward them). ﴿As they seek to hasten the good﴾: the phrase "as they seek to hasten the good" is placed in the position of "His hastening the good for them," to indicate the swiftness of His response to them regarding good, so that their seeking it is as though it were a hastening for them. Or it may be that the intended "evil" is something they sought to hasten, like their saying ﴿So rain down upon us stones from the heaven﴾. The sense of the sentence is: "And if Allah were to hasten the evil for mankind, hastening it as He hastens the good when they seek it with the same urgency as their seeking of good," so something was omitted from it, as the remaining part indicates it. ﴿Their term would have been decreed for them﴾: they would have been made to die and be destroyed. Ibn 'Amir and Ya'qub read (la-qada) with the active voice, its agent being Allah, the Exalted; and it was also read as "la-qadayna" (we would have decreed). ﴿So We leave those who do not expect the meeting with Us in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾: this is conjoined to a verb that has been omitted, which the conditional clause indicates, as if it were said: "But We do not hasten, nor do We decree, so We leave them to be granted respite and led on gradually."

(p-107) ﴿When harm touches man, he calls upon Us﴾ to remove it, sincerely devoting himself to Him in it. ﴿Lying on his side﴾: lying prone on his side, that is, reclining. ﴿Or sitting or standing﴾. The purpose of the alternation is to generalize the supplication to all states, or to all kinds of harm. ﴿But when We remove his harm from him, he passes on﴾: that is, he goes on in his way and persists in his disbelief, or he passes on from the position of supplication and does not return to it. ﴿As if he had never called upon Us﴾: as if he had never called upon Us. The word has been lightened and the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-sha'n) has been omitted, as in the verse of the poet:

*And a neck bright in hue... as if its two breasts were two ḥuqqān (small ivory boxes)*

﴿to a harm that had touched him﴾: to the removal of a harm. ﴿Thus﴾: like that adornment. ﴿It has been made attractive to the extravagant what they used to do﴾: namely, their immersion in appetites and their turning away from acts of worship.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 13–14:

﴿And We certainly destroyed the generations before you﴾, O people of Mecca. ﴿when they did wrong﴾, when they did wrong by denying [the messengers] and by using their faculties and limbs otherwise than as they should be used. ﴿And their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾, with the arguments that indicate their truthfulness. The phrase is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the waw [of the verb "they did wrong"], with qad implied, or it is coordinated (ʿatf) with "they did wrong". ﴿And they were not such as to believe﴾, and it was not fitting for them to believe, because of the corruption of their receptivity, God's forsaking of them, and His knowledge that they would die in their disbelief. The lam [in liyu'minu] serves to emphasize the negation. ﴿Thus﴾, like that recompense, which is their destruction on account of their denying the messengers and their persistence in it, to the point that it became certain that there was no benefit in granting them respite. ﴿We recompense the guilty people﴾, We recompense every guilty person, or "We recompense you." The apparent noun was placed in the position of the pronoun to indicate the perfection of their guilt and that they were exemplars of it.

﴿Then We made you successors in the land after them﴾, We made you successors in it after the generations We destroyed, as successors who are tested. ﴿So that We may see how you act﴾, whether you will do good or evil, so that We may deal with you according to the requirements of your deeds. The interrogative "how" (kayfa) is the object of "you act" (taʿmalūna); the meaning of interrogation prevents what precedes it from governing it. Its purpose is to indicate that what is taken into account in recompense are the aspects and manners of actions, not the actions in themselves; for this reason an act is sometimes good and sometimes ugly.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 15:

﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who do not expect to meet Us say﴾ meaning the polytheists. ﴿Bring a Qur'an other than this﴾, a different Book that we may recite, one in which there is nothing that we find improbable regarding resurrection, reward and punishment after death, or nothing that we dislike regarding the faults of our gods. ﴿Or change it﴾, by making in place of the verse containing such things another verse. Perhaps they asked this so that he would incline towards it and they would hold him to it. ﴿Say: It is not for me﴾, it is not right for me, ﴿to change it of my own accord﴾, from my own side. It is a verbal noun used as an adverb. The answer concerned only the changing because its impossibility entails the impossibility of bringing another Qur'an. ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me﴾. This is a reason for what is not for him to do, since one who follows another in a matter does not independently dispose of it. It is also an answer to the objection based on the abrogation (naskh) of some verses by others, and a rejection of what they raised with this question, namely that the Qur'an is his own speech and invention. For this reason he restricted the changing in the answer and called it disobedience, saying: ﴿Indeed I fear, if I disobey my Lord﴾, that is, by changing it, ﴿the punishment of a great day﴾. In this there is an indication that they deserved punishment by this suggestion.

(p-108) ﴿Say: "Had God willed [otherwise]"﴾ [i.e., had God willed otherwise]. ﴿I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made you aware of it﴾, nor would He have made you know of it through my tongue. It is also reported from Ibn Kathir that he read "wa-la-adraakum" (with the lam of emphasis), meaning: had God willed, He would indeed have recited it to you and made you know of it through the tongue of another than me. The meaning is that it is the truth from which there is no escape: had I not been sent with it, another would have been sent with it.

It was also read as "wa-la adra'akum" and "wa-la adra'tukum" with a hamza in both, according to the dialect of those who change an alif that replaced a yaa' into a hamza; or it is from al-dar' (ad-dar'), meaning repelling, i.e., "nor would I have made you disputants who repel me with argument by means of its recitation." The meaning is that the matter rests on the will of God Most High, not on my will, such that I would make it conform to what you desire. Then he confirmed this with His saying: ﴿So I have indeed remained among you a lifetime﴾, a period of forty years. ﴿Before it﴾, before the Qur'an, ﴿I neither recited it nor knew it﴾. This is an indication that the Qur'an is a miraculous marvel that breaks customary norms, for whoever lives among a people for forty years without practicing any learning, without seeing any scholar, without composing poetry or sermons, and then recites to them a book whose eloquence surpasses the eloquence of every orator and rises above all prose and verse, and which contains the rules of the sciences of the roots (usul) and the branches (furu'), and expresses the tales of the ancients and the narratives of the later generations as they truly are, is known to have received it from God Most High. ﴿Will you not then use your reason?﴾, i.e., will you not employ your intellects in reflection and contemplation upon it, so that you may know that it is nothing but from God.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 17–18:

﴿Who does greater wrong than one who fabricates a lie against Allah?﴾ This is implied by what they attributed to Him, as a metaphor (kinayah); or it is a charge of wrongdoing against the polytheists for their fabrication against Allah the Exalted in their saying that He has a associate and has offspring. ﴿Or denies His signs﴾, and so disbelieves in them. ﴿Indeed, the criminals will not succeed.﴾ ﴿And they worship, besides Allah, that which can neither harm them nor benefit them.﴾ For it is inanimate matter that has no power to benefit or harm, whereas the one worshipped ought to be one who rewards and punishes, so that worship of him brings the attainment of benefit or the averting of harm. ﴿And they say, "These are our intercessors with Allah."﴾ That is, the idols. ﴿They will intercede for us with Him in what concerns us of the affairs of this world or of the Hereafter, if there is a resurrection.﴾ It is as though they were doubtful about it, and this is from the extremity of their ignorance, in that they abandoned the worship of the One who originates, who harms and benefits, for the worship of that which is known with certainty neither to harm nor to benefit, on the assumption that it might perhaps intercede for them with Him. ﴿Say, "Will you inform Allah of what He does not know?"﴾ That is, will you tell Him? ﴿Of that which He does not know﴾, namely that He has an associate, or that these are intercessors with Him. What the One who knows all that is known does not know has no reality whatsoever. In this there is rebuke and mockery directed at them. ﴿In the heavens or on the earth.﴾ This is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the omitted returning pronoun, emphasizing the negation and alerting that what they worship besides Allah is either celestial or terrestrial, and there is nothing among the existents in either of them except that it is originated and subjugated, like them, and not fit to be associated with Him. ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.﴾ Above their associating, or above the associates whom they associate with Him. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read here, and in the two places at the beginning of al-Nahl and al-Rum, with the ta' (تُشْرِكُونَ, "you associate").

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 19–20:

﴿And mankind was not but one community﴾ — united upon the natural disposition (fitrah) or agreed upon the truth. This was in the era of Adam, peace be upon him, until Qabil (Cain) killed Habil (Abel), or after the Flood; or [they were] upon misguidance during a interval between the messengers. ﴿But they differed﴾ by following desires and falsehoods, or by the sending of the messengers, peace and blessings be upon them, so that one group followed them and another persisted [in disbelief]. ﴿And had it not been for a word that had preceded from your Lord﴾ — [namely] the postponement of judgment between them, or the decisive punishment between them, until the Day of Resurrection, for it is the Day of Decision and Recompense. ﴿It would have been decided between them﴾ immediately ﴿concerning that over which they differ﴾, by destroying the falsifier and preserving the one who is right.

﴿And they say, "Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord?"﴾ — i.e., from among the signs they had proposed. ﴿So say, "The unseen belongs only to Allah"﴾ — He alone has exclusive knowledge of it, so perhaps He knows that in sending the proposed signs there are corruptions which turn Him away from sending them. ﴿So wait﴾ for the descent of what you have proposed. ﴿Indeed, I am with you among those who wait﴾ for what Allah will do to you because of your denial of what was sent down to me of the great signs, and your proposing other than it.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 21:

﴿And when We let people taste mercy﴾ — health and abundance. ﴿after adversity has touched them﴾ — such as drought and sickness. ﴿Behold, they have a scheme against Our signs﴾ — by disparaging them and devising ways to repel them. It is said that the people of Makkah suffered drought for seven years, to the point that they nearly perished; then Allah had mercy on them with rain, and they set about disparaging the signs of Allah and plotting against His Messenger. ﴿Say: Allah is swifter in scheming﴾ than you. He has planned your punishment before you plan your deception. The swiftness in which they are surpassed is indicated by the word of sudden surprise (fa-idha, "behold") that falls as the response to the conditional particle idha. Scheming (makr) means concealing a plot. From Allah, the Exalted, it is either a gradual leading-on (istidraj) or a recompense for the scheming. ﴿Indeed, Our messengers record what you scheme﴾ — a confirmation of retribution and an alert that what they planned to conceal has not been hidden from the guardian angels, let alone from Allah, the Exalted. And from Ya'qub, it is read as yamkurun with a ya' so that it agrees with what precedes it.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 22–23:

﴿He it is who enables you to travel﴾ (yuseyyirukum): He carries you to travel and empowers you to do so. Ibn 'Amir read "yanshurukum" with the nun and the shin, from al-nashr (to spread out). ﴿On land and at sea, until when you are in the ships﴾ (al-fulk): in the vessels, ﴿and they sail with them﴾ (wa-jaraina bihim): with those on board. He shifted from direct address to the third person for emphasis, as if this were a reminder for others, so that they would marvel at their condition and censure them. ﴿With a fair wind﴾ (bi-rihin tayyibatin): gentle in its blowing. ﴿And they rejoice in it﴾ (wa-farihu biha): in that wind. ﴿Then there comes upon them﴾ (ja'athha): the response to "idha" (when), and the pronoun refers either to the ships or to the fair wind, in the sense of "they encountered it." ﴿A violent wind﴾ (rihun 'asif): possessing violent force, severe in its blowing. ﴿And the waves come upon them from every place﴾ (wa-ja'ahumu al-mawju min kulli makan): the waves come from every direction. ﴿And they think they are encompassed﴾ (wa-zannu annahum uhita bihim): they are destroyed, and the paths of escape are closed to them, like one whom the enemy has surrounded. ﴿They call upon God, making their religion sincerely His﴾ (da'awu Allaha mukhlisina lahu al-din): without associating anything with Him, due to the return of the natural disposition (al-fitra) and the removal of obstacles because of the severity of fear. It is a substitute (badal) for "zannu," a substitution of inclusion (badal ishtimal), because their supplication is a necessary consequence of their thinking.

﴿If You deliver us from this, we will surely be among the thankful﴾ (la'in anjaitana min hadhihi la-nakunanna mina al-shakirin): this is either by way of implying a speech (ala iradat al-qawl), or it is the object of "da'awu," since it is part of the speech.

﴿But when He delivered them﴾ (falamma anjahum): in response to their supplication. ﴿Behold, they committed injustice upon the earth﴾ (idha hum yabghuna fi al-ard): they suddenly engaged in corruption therein and hastened to what they had been doing. ﴿Without right﴾ (bi-ghayri al-haqq): acting wrongfully in it. This is a qualification excluding the destruction by Muslims of the lands of unbelievers, the burning of their crops and the uprooting of their trees, for these are corruption with right. ﴿O mankind, your injustice is only against yourselves﴾ (ya ayyuha al-nas innama baghyukum 'ala anfusikum): for its harm falls upon you, or it is against those like you, your fellow kind. ﴿An enjoyment of the worldly life﴾ (matA' al-hayat al-dunya): the benefit of the worldly life, which does not endure, while its punishment endures. It is in the nominative either as the predicate of "baghyukum," with "'ala anfusikum" as its complement, or as the predicate of an omitted subject, the implied meaning being "that is the enjoyment of the worldly life," and "'ala anfusikum" is the predicate of "baghyukum." Hafs read it in the accusative as an emphatic verbal noun (masdar muakkid), meaning "you enjoy the enjoyment of the worldly life," or as the object of "al-baghy," since it carries the meaning of seeking, in which case the prepositional phrase is its complement and the predicate is omitted, the implied meaning being "your injustice is an enjoyment of the worldly life, something to be feared, or error," or as the object of a verb indicated by "al-baghy," with "'ala anfusikum" as its predicate. ﴿Then to Us is your return﴾ (thumma ilayna marji'ukum): on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Then We will inform you of what you used to do﴾ (fanunabbi'ukum bima kuntum ta'malun): We will requite you for it.

﴿Indeed, the likeness of the worldly life﴾ is its wondrous state: how swiftly it passes away, and how its bounty departs after it has come, while people are deceived by it.

﴿like water that We sent down from the sky, whereupon the plants of the earth mingled with it﴾ so that they became entangled because of it, until some of them mixed with others. ﴿of what men and livestock eat﴾ from crops, herbs and grass. ﴿until, when the earth took on its adornment﴾ its beauty and splendor. ﴿and was decked out﴾ it adorned itself with the various kinds, forms and colors of plants, like a bride who takes on the colors of garments and ornaments and adorns herself with them. ﴿and was decked out﴾: its original form is tazayyanat, and it has been subjected to idgham (assimilation of two identical letters into one). It has also been read according to the original form as "wa-azyanat," in the form af'alat without i'lal (morphological alteration of weak letters), like aghyalat. The meaning is that it became full of ornament. It has also been read as "wazyanat," like ibyaddat. ﴿and its people thought that they had power over it﴾ that they were able to harvest it and gather its produce.

﴿Then Our command came upon it﴾ a calamity that destroyed its crops. ﴿by night or by day, and We made it﴾ We made its crops ﴿stubble﴾ resembling what has been reaped from its root. ﴿as though it had not flourished﴾ as though its crops had not flourished, that is, had not remained. The mudaf (the omitted noun, here "crops") is elided in both places for emphasis. It has also been read with the yā' (as yaghna), according to the original form. ﴿yesterday﴾ in the time that preceded it. This is a likeness of a short time. What is likened is the content of the account, namely the sudden disappearance of the greenness of the plants and their going away as debris after they had been fresh and dense, and had adorned the earth until their people coveted them and thought that they were safe from calamities. The particle of comparison (harf al-tashbih, "like") governs "yesterday" although it is not a comparison of noun to noun, because this is a composite simile (tashbih murakkab), in which the whole scene is compared with the whole scene.

﴿Thus do We detail the signs for a people who reflect﴾ for it is they who benefit from them.

﴿And God invites to the Abode of Peace﴾: the abode of safety from decay and calamity. Or it is the Abode of God, and the specification of this name is also for the sake of alerting to that. Or it is an abode in which God and the angels greet whoever enters it, and what is meant is Paradise. ﴿And He guides whom He wills﴾ with tawfiq (divine enabling). ﴿to a straight path﴾: it is its path, which is Islam and clothing oneself in the garment of taqwa (God-consciousness). In the generalising of the invitation and the restricting of guidance to His will, there is evidence that the command (al-amr) is other than the will (al-iradah), and that the one who persists in misguidance, God has not willed his right guidance.

﴿For those who have done good is the best (al-husna)﴾: the best reward. ﴿And an increase﴾: what exceeds the reward as a bounty, in accordance with His saying: ﴿and He will increase them from His bounty﴾. It was said: the best (al-husna) is the like of their good deeds, and the increase is ten times their like, up to seven hundred times and more. It was said: the increase is forgiveness from God and good pleasure (ridwan). It was said: the best is Paradise, and the increase is the meeting (with God).

﴿And neither dust nor humiliation shall cover their faces﴾: ﴿yarhaqu﴾ means it shall not cover them. ﴿Qatar﴾: a dust in which there is blackness. ﴿Nor humiliation﴾: disgrace. The meaning is: there shall not befall them what befalls the people of the Fire, or there shall not befall them what necessitates that, of grief and bad condition. ﴿Those are the companions of the Garden; therein they will abide forever﴾: remaining eternally, with no cessation in it and no ending of its bliss, unlike the world and its adornments.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 27–28:

(p-111) ﴿Those who have earned evil deeds—the recompense of an evil deed is one like it﴾. It is conjoined to his saying ﴿For those who did good is the best (reward)﴾, according to the view of those who permit (the construction) "In the house is Zayd and in the room is ʿAmr"; or ﴿those who﴾ (alladhīna) is a subject (mubtada'), and the predicate is ﴿the recompense of an evil deed is one like it﴾, with the implied supposition: "and the recompense of those who earned evil deeds is the recompense of an evil deed, one like it," i.e., that an evil deed be requited with an evil deed like it, without any addition to it. In this there is a warning that the addition is the bounty, or the multiplication, or ﴿as though their faces had been covered﴾, or ﴿those are the companions of the Fire﴾. What lies between them is a parenthetical interjection. So ﴿the recompense of an evil deed﴾ is a subject whose predicate is omitted, meaning: "then the recompense of an evil deed, with its like, is what will befall (them)," or "with its like" is by the addition of the preposition bi- (ba' al-ziyada), or by the supposition of an implied element: "with its like."

﴿And humiliation will cover them﴾; it is also read with the yā' (as yarhaquhum). ﴿They will have no protector from Allah against (Him). ﴾ No one will protect them from the wrath of Allah, or from the side of Allah, and from Him, as it is for the believers. ﴿As though their faces had been covered﴾: they were veiled. ﴿Their faces, as pieces of the night, dark﴾: due to the excess of their blackness and darkness. ﴿Dark﴾ (muẓlaman) is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from ﴿the night﴾, and its governing element is ﴿had been covered﴾, because it is the governing element of ﴿pieces﴾, which is qualified by the prepositional phrase; and the governing element of the qualified noun governs the qualifier, or the meaning of the verb in ﴿from the night﴾. Ibn Kathir, al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub read ﴿qiṭaʿan﴾ with a sukūn; according to this, ﴿muẓlaman﴾ may be an adjective of it or a circumstantial clause from it. ﴿Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever﴾: this is among what the Waʿīdiyya (the Threateners, i.e., Mu'tazilite-leaning proponents of the eternal punishment of the sinner) use as proof. The answer is that the verse concerns the disbelievers, since the evil deeds include disbelief and polytheism, and because ﴿those who did good﴾ encompasses the people of major sins among the people of the qibla, so the verse's counterpart does not encompass them.

**Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 29–30:**

﴿So Allah suffices as a witness between us and you﴾ — for He is the One who knows the true reality of the situation. ﴿Indeed, we were unaware of your worship﴾ — here ʾin is the lightened form (mukhaffafah) of the heavy (thaqilah) ʾinna, and the lam is the lam that distinguishes (al-lam al-fariqah) it from the negation. ﴿There﴾ — in that station. ﴿Every soul will experience what it has sent before﴾ — it will test (takhtabiru) what it has put forward of deeds, so that it witnesses (tuʿayinu) their benefit and their harm.

Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "tatlū" (تَتْلُو) from the recitation (al-tilawah), meaning it recites the record of what it has put forward; or from "al-tilw" (التِّلْو), meaning it follows its deed, and that leads it to Paradise or to Hell.

It was also read as "nabluū" (نَبْلُو) with the nun, with "kull" in the accusative case, and "mā" as a substitution (ibdal) from it. The meaning is: we test it, that is, we act toward it as one who tests its state and seeks to know its happiness and misery through knowing what it has sent before of its deeds. Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 31–32:

﴿Say: "Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth?"﴾ That is, from both of them together, since provision comes through heavenly causes and earthly materials. Or ﴿from﴾ each of them separately, as an expansion of blessing upon you. It has been said that "min" here is explanatory (li-bayan), with an elided noun, meaning "from the people of the heaven and the earth" (p-112). ﴿Or who owns hearing and sight?﴾ That is, or who is able to create them and shape them, or who protects them from afflictions, despite their multiplicity and the speed with which they are affected by the slightest thing. ﴿And who brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living?﴾ And who gives life and causes death; or who produces the animal from the drop of semen and the drop of semen from the animal. ﴿And who manages the affair?﴾ Who takes charge of the management of the affairs of the world; this is a generalization after a specification. ﴿They will say, "Allah."﴾ For they cannot be stubborn or obstinate about this, because of its great clarity. ﴿So say: "Will you not then be wary [of Allah]?"﴾ That is, will you not fear His punishment for associating with Him what shares with Him nothing of these things?

﴿Such is Allah, your true Lord.﴾ That is, the One who takes charge of these matters and who alone deserves worship, is your Lord, whose lordship is established, because He is the One who created you, gave you life, provided for you, and managed your affairs. ﴿So what is there after the truth but error?﴾ This is a rhetorical question of denial: there is nothing after the truth but error; whoever transgresses the truth, which is the worship of Allah the Exalted, falls into error. ﴿How then are you turned away?﴾ From the truth toward error.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 35–36:

﴿Say: Is there any of your associate-gods who guides to the truth?﴾ By establishing the proofs and sending the messengers, upon them be blessings and peace, and by granting success (tawfiq) for reflection (nazar) and contemplation (tadabbur). "Hada" (to guide) is transitive with "ila" (to), as it is with "li" (for) when it implies the meaning of "intiha'" (arriving at); it is transitive with "li" to indicate that the destination is the ultimate goal of guidance, and that it was not directed towards it by mere chance. For this reason, that which is attributed to God the Exalted is also transitive with it. ﴿Say: God guides to the truth. Is then He who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or he who does not find guidance unless he is guided?﴾ The phrase "lā yahiddi" is from their saying "hudiya bi-nafsihi" when he finds guidance by himself; or it means: he does not guide others unless God guides him. This is the condition of the most noble of their associate-gods, such as the angels, al-Masih, and 'Uzayr. Ibn Kathir and Warsh, on the authority of Nafi', and Ibn 'Amir read ﴿yahdi﴾ with a fatha on the ha' and a shadda on the dal. Ya'qub and Hafs (read it) with a kasra, with shadda, and the original form is "yahtadi", which was assimilated; the ha' took the fatha by the vowel of the ta', or was given a kasra due to the meeting of two sukun. Abu Bakr narrated ﴿yahdi﴾ with the ya' imitating the ha'. Abu 'Amr read with simple assimilation (al-idgham al-mujarrad) and did not mind the meeting of two sukun, because the assimilated letter is treated as vowelled. The same is related from Nafi' by the narration of Qalun. It is also read "illa an yahdiya" for emphasis (al-mubalagha). ﴿What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾ with that which clear reason requires its falsehood. ﴿And most of them do not follow﴾ in what they believe. ﴿except conjecture﴾ resting upon empty imaginings and corrupt analogies, such as analogizing the unseen to the seen and the Creator to the created on the basis of some slight, imagined similarity. By "most" is meant all of them, or those among them who ascribe to discernment and reflection and do not content themselves with pure imitation. ﴿Indeed, conjecture avails nothing against the truth﴾ of knowledge and belief (p-113) the truth. ﴿anything﴾ in the sense of providing sufficiency. It is permissible for it to be the object, and ﴿against the truth﴾ to be a circumstantial clause (hal) from it. In this is evidence that acquiring knowledge in the fundamentals (usul) is obligatory, and that relying on imitation and conjecture is not permissible. ﴿Indeed, God is Knowing of what they do﴾ a warning against their following of conjecture and their turning away from the clear proof.

**Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 39:**

﴿Nay, they denied﴾ — rather, they hastened to denial. ﴿that which they did not encompass in knowledge﴾ — of the Qur'an, at the very first hearing of it, before they had reflected upon its verses and comprehended the knowledge of its matter; or [it means] that which they were ignorant of and had not encompassed in knowledge, namely the mention of the Resurrection and the recompense and all else that contradicts their religion. ﴿And its interpretation has not yet come to them﴾ — they had not yet arrived at its interpretation, nor had their minds reached its meanings; or [it means] the interpretation of what it contains of reports of the unseen had not yet come to them, so that it might become clear to them whether it is true or false. The meaning is that the Qur'an is inimitable in respect of both its wording and its meaning, and then they hastened to deny it before they had reflected upon its composition and examined its meaning. The sense of expectation in "lammā" (not yet) is that its inimitability became manifest to them in the end, when the challenge was repeated to them and they increased their strength in opposing it, but it was diminished in comparison; or [it means] when they witnessed the occurrence of what it had reported, in conformity with its reports, many times, yet they did not desist from denial, out of obstinacy and stubbornness. ﴿Thus did those before them deny﴾ — their prophets. ﴿So see how was the end of the wrongdoers﴾ — this contains a warning to them of the same punishment with which those before them were punished.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 40–41:

﴿And among them﴾ — that is, among the deniers. ﴿are those who believe in it﴾ — that is, those who affirm it in their hearts and know that it is true, but are stubborn; or those who (p-114) will come to believe in it and repent of disbelief. ﴿And among them are those who do not believe in it﴾ — in their hearts, due to their extreme dullness and little reflection; or regarding what is yet to come, but they will die upon disbelief. ﴿And your Lord knows best the corrupters﴾ — that is, the stubborn ones or the persistent ones.

﴿And if they deny you﴾ — that is, if they persist in denying you after the proof has been established against them. ﴿Then say: "For me is my deed, and for you is your deed"﴾ — so disassociate yourself from them, for you have given them an excuse. The meaning is: for me is the recompense of my deed, and for you is the recompense of your deed, whether it be true or false. ﴿You are free of what I do, and I am free of what you do﴾ — you will not be held accountable for my deed, nor will I be held accountable for your deed. Because of what this may suggest of turning away from them and leaving them to their way, it has been said that it is abrogated by the verse of the sword (āyat al-sayf).

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 40–41:

﴿And among them﴾ — that is, among the deniers. ﴿are those who believe in it﴾ — that is, those who affirm it in their hearts and know that it is true, but are stubborn; or those who (p-114) will come to believe in it and repent of disbelief. ﴿And among them are those who do not believe in it﴾ — in their hearts, due to their extreme dullness and little reflection; or regarding what is yet to come, but they will die upon disbelief. ﴿And your Lord knows best the corrupters﴾ — that is, the stubborn ones or the persistent ones.

﴿And if they deny you﴾ — that is, if they persist in denying you after the proof has been established against them. ﴿Then say: "For me is my deed, and for you is your deed"﴾ — so disassociate yourself from them, for you have given them an excuse. The meaning is: for me is the recompense of my deed, and for you is the recompense of your deed, whether it be true or false. ﴿You are free of what I do, and I am free of what you do﴾ — you will not be held accountable for my deed, nor will I be held accountable for your deed. Because of what this may suggest of turning away from them and leaving them to their way, it has been said that it is abrogated by the verse of the sword (āyat al-sayf).

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 42–43:

﴿And among them are those who listen to you﴾ when you recite the Qur'an and teach the laws (sharai'), but they do not accept it, like the deaf man who does not hear at all. ﴿Can you make the deaf hear?﴾ That is, can you make them hear? ﴿Even though they do not understand﴾ That is, even if their deafness is compounded by their not reasoning. In this there is an alert that the reality of listening to speech is grasping the intended meaning of it, and for this reason animals are not described as listening to it. This [grasping] cannot be achieved except by using sound reason in reflecting upon it. Their intellects, since they were impaired by the opposition of illusion (wahm) and the following of habit and blind imitation (taqlid), made it impossible for them to be made to comprehend the wisdoms and the subtle meanings. So they did not benefit from the recitation of words to them beyond what animals benefit from the speech of one who calls out (al-nпа'iq).

﴿And among them are those who look at you﴾ they witness the proofs of your prophethood, but they do not believe you. ﴿Can you guide the blind?﴾ That is, can you guide them? ﴿Even though they do not see﴾ Even if lack of insight is added to lack of sight. For the purpose of sight is consideration (i'tibar) and discernment (istibsar), and the foundation of that is insight (basirah). For this reason the blind man perceives the discerning person and grasps what the sighted fool does not perceive. The verse serves as a reason for the command to disavow them and turn away from them.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 44–45:

﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong the people at all﴾ by depriving them of their senses and their intellects. ﴿But it is the people who wrong themselves﴾ by corrupting them and forfeiting their benefits for themselves. In this is evidence that the servant has acquisition (kasb), and that he is not wholly deprived of choice (ikhtiyar), as the Mujbira (Compulsionists) claimed. It is also possible that this is a warning to them, meaning that what befalls them on the Day of Resurrection of punishment is justice from Allah, Who does not wrong them with it, but they wronged themselves by committing its causes. Abu 'Amr and al-Kisa'i read it with the lightened form (al-takhfif) and the nominative (raf') on (al-nas, "the people").

﴿And [mention] the Day He will gather them, [it will be] as if they had not remained [in the world] except an hour of the day﴾ They will consider the duration of their stay in the world, or in the graves, to be short because of the terror of what they see. The comparative clause is in the position of a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning: He will gather them, likened to those who did not remain except an hour. Or it is a description of "a day," and its returning pronoun is omitted, its estimate being: "as if they had not remained before it." Or it is an adjunct to an omitted verbal noun, meaning: a gathering as if they had not remained before it. ﴿They will recognize one another among themselves﴾ Some of them will know others, as if they had not been separated except briefly. This is the first thing when they are raised, and then recognition ends because of the severity of the matter upon them. This is another circumstantial clause, supposed (muqaddarah), or an explanation of His saying: ﴿as if they had not remained﴾, or it is related to the adverbial phrase, and the estimate is: they will recognize one another on the Day He gathers them.

﴿Those who denied the meeting with Allah have certainly lost﴾ This is a resumptive statement (isti'naf) as testimony to their loss and an expression of wonder at it. It is also possible that it is a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in (yataʿarafun), with the sense of saying. ﴿And they were not guided﴾ to the ways of using the aids they were given in acquiring knowledge; so they acquired through them ignorances that led them to ruin and everlasting punishment.

**Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 46–47:**

(p-115) "Whether We show you some of what We threaten them with" — We let you see it — "[some of] the punishment, during your lifetime, as We showed it to you on the Day of Badr. "Or We cause you to die" before We show it to you, "then to Us is their return," so We will show it to them in the Hereafter. The answer to "We cause you to die" is "then to Us is their return," and the answer to "We show you" is omitted, like "then that is [sufficient]." "Then Allah is Witness over what they do" — He will requite them for it. He mentioned the witnessing and intended its result and consequence, and for this reason He placed it after the return with "then" (thumma). Or it means: one who will render His testimony concerning their deeds on the Day of Resurrection.

"And for every community there is a messenger" from the past nations, "who is sent to them to call them to the truth. "So when their messenger comes" with the clear proofs and they deny him, "judgment is passed between them" — between the Messenger and his deniers — "with justice," with fairness, "so the Messenger is saved and the deniers are destroyed."

"And they are not wronged." It has also been said that its meaning is: for every community on the Day of Resurrection there is a messenger to whom they are attributed. "So when their messenger comes" to the place of standing, to bear witness against them concerning disbelief and belief, He judges between them by saving the believers and punishing the disbelievers, according to His saying: "And the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and judgment will be passed between them."

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 48–49:

﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾ (They say this) out of disbelief in it (istib'ad) and mockery of it (istihza'). ﴿If you are truthful﴾ is an address from them to the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 50–51:

﴿Say: "Tell me, if His punishment comes upon you by night or by day, what is it that the criminals would hasten to have it?"﴾ "Which" (alladhi) refers to the punishment you are hastening for. "By night" (bayatan) means at the time of nightly sleep and occupation with rest. "Or by day" (naharan) means at the time when you are occupied with seeking your livelihood. "What is it that the criminals would hasten to have of it?" means: what part of the punishment is it that they are hastening for, when all of it is disagreeable and does not suit hastening toward it? The phrase is connected to "Tell me" (ara'aytum), because it carries the meaning of "inform me." The word "the criminals" (al-mujrimun) has been placed in the position of the pronoun to indicate that, because of their crime, they ought to be fearful of the coming of the punishment, not to hasten it. The answer to the conditional is omitted, and it is: "you would regret having hastened," or "you would recognize its error." It is also permissible that the answer be "what" (madha), as in your saying, "If I come to you, what will you give me?" and the clause is then connected to "Tell me" (ara'aytum), or to His saying:

﴿Is it then, when it has occurred, that you will believe in it?﴾ meaning: if His punishment comes upon you, you will believe in it after its occurrence, at a time when belief will not benefit you. "What is it that they would hasten" is a parenthetical clause, and the entry of the interrogative particle upon "then" (thumma) is to deny the delay. ﴿Now?﴾ On the intention of speech, meaning: it will be said to them, when they believe after the punishment has occurred, "Now you believe in it?" It is related from Nafi' that he read "Alan" with the hamza removed and its vowel placed on the lam. ﴿And you were hastening for it, denying and mocking.﴾

(p-116) ﴿وَيَسْتَنْبِئُونَكَ﴾ [And they ask you to inform them], that is, they ask you for information. ﴿أحَقٌّ هُوَ﴾ [Is it true?], that is, is what you say of the promise or of the claim to prophethood true, or is it false, which you say in jest? This was said by Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab when he came to Makkah. It has also been said that it is for denial (inkār), and this is supported by the fact that it was recited as "Āl-ḥaqqu huwa" (آلْحَقُّ هو), since this contains an implicit insinuation that it is false. The word *aḥaqqu* is a mubtada' (subject of a nominal sentence), and the pronoun *huwa* is raised by it, serving in place of the predicate (khabar); or *aḥaqqu* is a fronted predicate (khabar muqaddam), and the clause is in the position of the accusative (naṣb) governed by (يَسْتَنْبِئُونَكَ). ﴿قُلْ إي ورَبِّي إنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ﴾ [Say: "Yes, by my Lord, indeed it is true"], that is, the punishment is certainly to come, or what I have claimed is established. Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 54:

﴿And if every soul that wronged⁠—﴾ by associating partners with God or by transgressing against others⁠—﴿had whatever is on the earth of its treasures and its wealth, it would surely offer it as ransom⁠﴾; it would make it a ransom for itself from the punishment. This is from their saying "iftada-hu" (he ransomed him), which means "fada-hu" (he ransomed him). ﴿And they will conceal the regret when they see the punishment﴾, because they will be struck dumb by what they witness of the terrible and dreadful nature of the matter, which they had not expected, so they will be unable to speak. It has also been said that "asarru al-nadamah" means they will keep the regret pure (akhlasuha), because concealing it is keeping it pure; or because one says "sarra al-shay'" to mean its choicest part, since it is hidden and held dear. It has also been said that they will display it, from the expression "asarra al-shay'" and "ashharahu" when he made it apparent. ﴿And judgment will be given between them with justice, and they will not be wronged﴾. This is not a repetition, because the first refers to the judgment between the prophets and their deniers, and the second to the requital of the polytheists for their polytheism, or to the adjudication between the wrongdoers and the wronged. The pronoun refers to them only because the wrongdoing points to them.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 55–56:

﴿Surely, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth.﴾ This is an affirmation of His power (qudrah) to reward and to punish (ithabah wa-'iqab). ﴿Surely, the promise of Allah is true.﴾ What He has promised of reward and punishment will certainly come to pass, with no failure in it. ﴿But most of them do not know.﴾ Because they do not know, owing to the deficiency of their intellects, except (what is) apparent of the life of this world.

﴿He gives life and causes death.﴾ In this world. So He is able to do both in the Hereafter, because the one who is capable by His very essence (al-qadir li-dhatihi) does not lose His power, and the substrate (al-maddah) that is receptive by its very nature to life and death will have them forever. ﴿And to Him you will be returned.﴾ By death or by resurrection (nushur).

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 57–58:

﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you an admonition from your Lord, and a cure for what is in the breasts, and guidance and mercy for the believers.﴾ That is: there has certainly come to you a Book comprehensive of practical wisdom (*al-hikmah al-'amaliyyah*, wisdom concerning action), which reveals the goodness and ugliness of deeds, encourages toward the good and deters from the ugly, and of theoretical wisdom (*al-hikmah al-nazariyyah*, wisdom concerning belief), which is a cure for what is in the breasts of doubts and corrupt belief, and guidance to the truth and certainty, and mercy for the believers, since it was revealed to them and by it they were saved from the darknesses of error to the light of faith, and their places were exchanged from the levels of the fires to ascending stages of the degrees of the Gardens. The indefiniteness here is for magnification.

﴿Say: "By the grace of God and His mercy"﴾, by the sending down of the Qur'an. The *ba'* is connected to a verb which is explained by His saying: ﴿So in that let them rejoice﴾, for the demonstrative is in the position of a pronoun. Its estimate is: "By God's grace and His mercy, let them take care," or "let them rejoice; so in that let them rejoice." The benefit of this repetition is emphasis and clarification after generality, and making the grace and mercy specifically the object of rejoicing, or of a verb indicated by ﴿there has certainly come to you﴾. "That" refers to its source, i.e., "so by its coming let them rejoice." The *fa'* carries the meaning of a condition, as if it were said: "If they rejoice in anything, then in these two let them rejoice." Or it is for linking to what precedes, and indicating that the coming of the comprehensive Book combining these attributes necessitates joy. Its repetition is for emphasis, like his saying:

*"And when I perish, then at that time, wail."*

And it is reported from Ya'qub: « فَلْتَفْرَحُوا» with the *ta'* according to the original form, which was abandoned; and it has been narrated as marfu' (nominative). It is supported by the fact that « فافْرَحُوا» was read.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 57–58:

﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you an admonition from your Lord, and a cure for what is in the breasts, and guidance and mercy for the believers.﴾ That is: there has certainly come to you a Book comprehensive of practical wisdom (*al-hikmah al-'amaliyyah*, wisdom concerning action), which reveals the goodness and ugliness of deeds, encourages toward the good and deters from the ugly, and of theoretical wisdom (*al-hikmah al-nazariyyah*, wisdom concerning belief), which is a cure for what is in the breasts of doubts and corrupt belief, and guidance to the truth and certainty, and mercy for the believers, since it was revealed to them and by it they were saved from the darknesses of error to the light of faith, and their places were exchanged from the levels of the fires to ascending stages of the degrees of the Gardens. The indefiniteness here is for magnification.

﴿Say: "By the grace of God and His mercy"﴾, by the sending down of the Qur'an. The *ba'* is connected to a verb which is explained by His saying: ﴿So in that let them rejoice﴾, for the demonstrative is in the position of a pronoun. Its estimate is: "By God's grace and His mercy, let them take care," or "let them rejoice; so in that let them rejoice." "That" refers to its source, i.e., "so by its coming let them rejoice." The *fa'* carries the meaning of a condition, as if it were said: "If they rejoice in anything, then in these two let them rejoice." Or it is for linking to what precedes, and indicating that the coming of the comprehensive Book combining these attributes necessitates joy. Its repetition is for emphasis, like his saying:

**Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on Surah 10, verses 59–60:**

﴿Say: Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision﴾. The provision is described as "sent down" because it is decreed in the heaven and obtained through means from it. The phrase *mā* (ما) is in the accusative position, either governed by ﴿sent down﴾ (*anzala*, أنزَلَ) or by ﴿Have you considered﴾ (*ara'aytum*, أرَأيْتُم), since the latter carries the sense of "tell me" (*akhbirūnī*, أخْبِرُونِي). The word ﴿to you﴾ (*lakum*, لَكُم) indicates that what is meant is what is lawful. For this reason, He rebuked them for partitioning it, saying: ﴿then you made of it what is unlawful and lawful﴾, like His words: ﴿These are cattle and tilth, forbidden﴾ [and with regard to His saying, exalted is He] ﴿What is in the wombs of these cattle is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives﴾. ﴿Say: Has God permitted you﴾ to forbid and to make lawful, so that you say this by His command? ﴿Or do you invent about God﴾ by attributing that to Him? The disjunctive (*munfaṣilah*, مُنْفَصِلَة) may be connected (*muttaṣilah*, مُتَّصِلَة) to ﴿Have you considered﴾, with ﴿Say﴾ repeated for emphasis, and the interrogation may be for denial. Here *am* (أم) is disconnected (*munqaṭi'ah*, مُنْقَطِعَة), and the meaning of the hamzah (*hamzah*, الهَمْزَة) in it is affirmation of their fabrication against God.

﴿And what will be the thought of those who invent falsehood against God﴾, that is, what will their assumption be? ﴿on the Day of Resurrection﴾: will they suppose that they will not be recompensed for it? It is in the accusative governed by the verb "think" (*al-ẓann*, الظَّنّ), and what indicates this is that it has been recited in the past tense (*al-māḍī*, الماضِي), because it is certain to occur. The vagueness of the threat conveys a great warning. ﴿Indeed, God is full of bounty toward the people﴾, in that He has blessed them with reason and guided them by sending the messengers and revealing the scriptures. ﴿But most of them do not give thanks﴾ for this blessing.

ۚ﴿And you are not engaged in any affair﴾ — you are not in any matter (sha'n). Its root is with a hamza, from "sha'anta sha'nahu," meaning "I intended his intention." The pronoun in ﴿And you do not recite from it﴾ refers to the affair, because the recitation of the Qur'an magnifies the station of the Messenger, or because the recitation is for a matter, so the implied sense is "for its sake." The object of "tatlu" (recite) is ﴿any Qur'an﴾, where "min" is either partitive (tab'idiyyah) or redundant (zaidah) for emphasizing the negation, or it is attached to "Qur'an." Its (the object's) pronoun being placed before its mention and then explained is a form of magnification of it, or of God. ﴿Nor do you do any deed﴾ — a generalization of the address after it was specified to the one who is their head (the Prophet ﷺ). For this reason, it is mentioned where something of grandeur is specified, and mentioned where it generalizes to what includes the great and the small. ﴿But We are witnesses over you﴾ — watchful observers who are aware of it. ﴿When you are engaged in it﴾ — you immerse yourselves in it and rush into it. ﴿And not escapes from your Lord﴾ — nor is it far from Him, nor is it hidden from His knowledge. Al-Kisa'i read the zay (ز) with a kasra here and in "Saba'." ﴿The weight of an atom's particle﴾ — the weight of a small ant or a mote of dust. ﴿On the earth or in the heaven﴾ — that is, in existence and possibility, for the common people do not know of any possible thing other than these two that is not within them or connected to them. The earth is mentioned first because the discourse concerns the state of its inhabitants, and the purpose of it is the proof of the comprehensiveness of His knowledge of them. ﴿Nor smaller than that, nor greater, but it is in a clear Book﴾ — a separate statement confirming what precedes it; "lā" is negating, "asghara" is its subject, and "fī kitābin" is its predicate. Ḥamzah and Ya'qub read it in the nominative (marfu') as a beginning and predicate, and whoever takes it as a conjunction to the wording of "mithqal dharrah" and makes the fatḥa a substitute for the kasra due to the prohibition of declension, or to its position together with the preposition, makes the exception disjunctive (munqati'). The "Book" here means the Preserved Tablet.

﴿Indeed, the allies of Allah﴾, those who take Him as their ally through obedience, and whom He takes as His allies through honour. ﴿No fear shall be upon them﴾ of any harm befalling them.

﴿Nor shall they grieve﴾ over the loss of something they hoped for. The verse is like a general statement (mujmal) whose explanation is His words: ﴿Those who believed and used to be mindful of Allah﴾. It is also said that ﴿those who believed and used to be mindful of Allah﴾ is an explanation (bayan) of their being allies of Him.

﴿For them is good news in the life of this world﴾, which is what He has given good news of to the God-fearing in His Book and through the tongue of His Prophet (ﷺ), and what He shows them of good dreams, and what unveilings (mukashafat) occur to them, and the good news of the angels at the time of death. ﴿And in the Hereafter﴾: by the angels receiving them, greeting them and giving them good news of success and honour. This is an explanation of His being their ally.

The position (mahall) of ﴿those who believed﴾ is either in the accusative (nasb) or the nominative (raf') for the sake of praise (madh), or as a description (wasf) of the allies, or as the inchoative (mubtada'), whose predicate (khabar) is ﴿for them is good news﴾.

﴿There is no alteration in the words of Allah﴾, meaning there is no change in His sayings and no breaking of His promises. ﴿That﴾ refers to their being given good news in both abodes. ﴿That is the great success﴾. This sentence and the one before it form a parenthetical clause (i'tiraḍ) to confirm the good news and magnify its importance, and it is not a requirement that a sentence connected to what precedes it should follow it.

"And let not their speech grieve you" — their polytheism, their denial, and their threats.

Nafi' read it as "yuhzinka" (from the fourth form, ahzana), while the others read "yahzunka"; both have the same meaning.

"Indeed, all might belongs to God" — this is a resumptive sentence (isti'naf) with the sense of giving a reason. The reading with the fatha on "inna" (anna) supports this: it is as if it were said, "Do not grieve over their words and do not concern yourself with them, because all dominance belongs to God; none other possesses any share of it. So He subdues them and gives you victory over them."

"He is the All-Hearing" — of their sayings. "The All-Knowing" — of their resolves, so He will repay them for them.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 66–67:

﴿Verily, to Allah belongs whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth﴾, from among the angels and the two weighty ones (humans and jinn). And if these, who are the most noble of possible beings, are servants, none of them being fit for lordship, then what does not understand is more deserving that it should not have a rival or a partner. So this is like evidence for His saying: ﴿And those who call upon other than Allah do not follow partners﴾, meaning: partners in reality, even though they call them partners. It is also permissible that ﴿partners﴾ is the object of "yad'una" (they call upon), and the object of "yattabi'u" (they follow) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. ﴿They follow nothing but conjecture﴾, meaning: they do not follow certainty; they only follow their own supposition that these are partners. It is also permissible that "ma" be interrogative, governed in the accusative by "yattabi'u" (follow), or relative, conjoined to "man" (whoever). It has been read "tad'una" (you call) with the second-person ta', and the meaning is: "What do those whom you call partners, from among the angels and the prophets, follow?" That is, they do not follow anything but Allah, and do not worship other than Him. So what is with you that you do not follow them in it? Like His saying: ﴿Those whom they call upon seek the means of approach to their Lord﴾. Thus this is a rebuke after proof, and what follows is turned away from address to explain their basis and the source of their opinion.

﴿And they are only guessing﴾, meaning: they lie concerning what they attribute to Allah, or they estimate and conjecture that these are partners, an estimation that is false.

﴿It is He who made the night for you that you may rest therein, and the day to see by.﴾ This is an alert to the perfection of His power and the magnitude of His blessing, and that He alone is the one who has made these two; so that they may be shown His uniqueness in deserving worship. He said "mubsiran" (to see by) and did not say "li-tubsiru fihi" (that you may see therein), to distinguish between the mere time-container and the container that is a cause. ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for a people who hear﴾, hearing with reflection and consideration.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 68:

﴿They said: "Allah has taken a son."﴾ That is, adopted him. ﴿Glory be to Him!﴾ It is a declaration of His transcendence above adoption, for adoption is only valid from one for whom a son can be conceived, and an expression of wonder at their foolish statement. ﴿He is the Self-Sufficient (al-Ghani)﴾ is a reason for declaring Him transcendent, for taking a son is caused by need. ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ is an affirmation of His self-sufficiency. ﴿You have no authority for this﴾ is a negation of any contrary evidence to the proof He has established, as an intensification of their ignorance and a confirmation of the falsehood of their statement. The phrase ﴿for this﴾ (bihadha) is connected to ﴿authority﴾ (sultan), or is a qualifier of it, or connected to ﴿you have﴾ (indakum), as if it were said: "You have no authority in this." ﴿Do you say about Allah what you do not know?﴾ is a rebuke and reproach for their disagreement and ignorance. In it is evidence that every statement without proof is ignorance, that beliefs必 require a decisive proof (qati'), and that imitation (taqlid) in them is not permissible.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 69–70:

﴿Say: Indeed, those who fabricate lies against Allah will not succeed.﴾ By ascribing a son to Him and attributing a partner to Him. ﴿Will not succeed﴾ means they will not be saved from the Fire, nor will they attain Paradise.

﴿A brief enjoyment in this world﴾ is the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: their fabrication is a brief enjoyment in this world, by which they maintain their leadership in disbelief, or their life, or their turning about (in affairs). Or, "a brief enjoyment" is the subject, and its predicate is omitted, meaning: for them there is enjoyment in this world. ﴿Then to Us is their return﴾ by death, whereupon they will meet everlasting wretchedness. ﴿Then We shall make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve﴾ — because of their disbelief.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 71:

﴿And recite to them the news of Noah﴾: his account with his people. ﴿When he said to his people: "O my people, if my standing (maqam) and my reminding you of the signs of God is grievous to you"﴾: it was great upon you and burdensome. "My standing (maqam)" means my self, as when you say "I did such-and-such because of the place (makan) of so-and-so"; or it means my dwelling and residing among you for a long period; or my standing up (qiyam) to the call.

﴿And my reminding (tadhkiri) you﴾: of them. ﴿with the signs of God. Upon God I have relied﴾: I have trusted in Him. ﴿So resolve upon your affair﴾: determine upon it firmly.

﴿And your associates (shurakaa'akum)﴾: that is, together with your associates. The reading in the nominative supports this, as a conjunction with the attached pronoun, and it was permissible without emphasis because of the separation. It is also said that it is conjoined to ﴿your affair (amrakum)﴾ by omitting the genitive-governing noun, i.e., "and the affair of your associates." It is also said that it is in the accusative by a verb omitted, its estimate being "and call upon your associates," and it has been read so. It is narrated from Nafi' (fa-ajmi'u) from the root j-m-', and the meaning is: he commanded them to resolve or to unite upon the intent to him and to strive to destroy him in whatever way they could, with confidence in God and with little concern for them. ﴿Then let not your affair be﴾: in regard to my intent. ﴿upon you a gloom (ghummah)﴾: concealed; and make it manifest and open. It derives from "he covered it" (ghammahu) when he concealed it. Or: "let not your situation be a source of grief upon you if you destroy me and rid yourselves of the burden of my standing and my reminding." ﴿Then carry out (iqdu)﴾: discharge. ﴿to me﴾: that matter which you intend against me. It was also read "thumma afdu ilayya" with the fa', meaning: reach me with your evil, or come forth to me, from afda, when one goes out into the open space (fada'). ﴿And do not give me respite﴾: do not delay me.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 72–73:

(p-120) ﴿But if you turn away﴾: you turn away from my admonition. ﴿Then I have not asked of you any wage﴾ which would necessitate your turning away because of its burden upon you and your suspicion of me on its account, or which would be lost to me because of your turning away. ﴿My wage is only from Allah﴾: my reward for the call and the admonition. ﴿Only upon Allah﴾, to whom you have no connection, who will reward me for it, whether you believe or turn away. ﴿And I have been commanded to be among the Muslims﴾: those who submit to His judgment, not opposing His command nor hoping for anything other than Him.

﴿So they denied him﴾: they persisted in denying him after he had established the proof against them and made clear that their turning away was nothing but obstinacy and rebellion. Undoubtedly the word of punishment was justified against them. ﴿So We delivered him﴾ from the drowning. ﴿And those with him in the ark﴾, and they were eighty. ﴿And We made them successors﴾ to those destroyed by it. ﴿And We drowned those who denied Our signs﴾ by the flood. ﴿So see how was the end of those who were warned﴾: a magnification of what befell them, a warning to whoever denies the Messenger (ﷺ), and a consolation to him.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 74:

﴿Then We sent﴾ means: We sent. ﴿After him﴾ means: after Noah. ﴿Messengers to their peoples﴾ means: every messenger to his own people. ﴿And they came to them with clear signs﴾ means: with the evident miracles that confirmed their claims. ﴿Yet they were not such as to believe﴾ means: it was not fitting for them to believe, owing to the severity of their obstinacy in disbelief and God's abandonment of them. ﴿Because of what they had denied before﴾ means: by reason of their habituation to rejecting the truth and their being trained in it before God sent the messengers, peace be upon them. ﴿Thus do We seal the hearts of the transgressors﴾ means: through their being forsaken, because of their immersion in misguidance and their following of what was familiar. In such instances there is evidence that actions occur by the power of God Most High and the acquisition (kasb) of the servant, and the verification of this has already been discussed.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 75–76:

﴿Then We sent after them﴾ after these messengers, ﴿Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and his chiefs with Our signs﴾ with the nine signs.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (*Anwar al-Tanzil*) on surah 10, verse 77:

﴿Moses said, "Do you say of the truth when it has come to you…"﴾ "Surely this is magic," so the quoted speech (al-mahkiy al-maqul) is omitted, because what precedes it indicates it. It is not permissible for it to be [the quoted speech]. ﴿Is this magic?﴾ Because they had already made a firm statement (batta al-qawl). Rather, it is a resumptive sentence (isti'naf) that rejects what they said. Unless the interrogative here is for affirmation (taqrir), and the quoted speech is the implied meaning of their words. It is also possible that the meaning of ﴿Do you say of the truth…﴾ is "Do you blame it for what they say: so-and-so fears gossip (al-qala)?" Like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We heard a young man mention them﴾ (21:60), and so it dispenses with the object.

﴿And the magicians do not prosper﴾ is part of Moses's speech, to indicate that this is not magic. For if it were magic, it would have vanished and would not have nullified the magic of the magicians. Also, one who knows that the magician does not prosper does not practise magic. Or it is part of their speech, if "Is this magic?" is taken as quoted speech, as though they had said: "Have you come to us with magic, seeking by it prosperity?" And the magicians do not prosper.(p-121)

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 78–80:

﴿They said: "Have you come to us to turn us away﴾ from what we found our fathers upon?" That is, to divert us (litaftina: li-tasrifana). Al-laft (turning) and al-fatl (twisting) are brothers in meaning. ﴿from what we found our fathers upon﴾ of worshipping idols.

﴿And that greatness (al-kibriya') may be yours in the land﴾: al-mulk (kingship) in it, and it was so called because kings are characterized by pride (al-kibr), or because of domineering over people by making them subservient. ﴿We are not going to believe you﴾: we are not going to be believers (bi-musaddiqin) in what you have brought.

﴿And Pharaoh said: "Bring me every learned sorcerer"﴾ Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited bi-kulli sahharin (every skilled sorcerer). ﴿learned﴾: skilled (haziq) in it. ﴿So when the sorcerers came, Moses said to them: "Throw what you are going to throw."﴾
