Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 81–82:

﴿When they had cast, Musa said: "What you have brought is magic."﴾ That is, what you have brought is magic, not what Pharaoh and his people called magic. Abu 'Amr recited (as-sihru) with the *raf'* (nominative) on the basis that *ma* is an interrogative (*istifhamiyyah*, a question word), in the nominative as the subject (*mubtada'*, grammatical subject) with *ji'tum bihi* as its predicate (*khabar*, the predicate), and *as-sihru* as an appositive substitute (*badal*) for it, or as the predicate of an omitted subject, whose sense is "Is it magic?", or as a subject whose predicate is omitted, meaning "The magic is what it is." It is also permissible for *ma* to be in the accusative, governed by a verb that is explained by what follows it, with the sense "Whatever you have brought." ﴿Indeed, Allah will surely nullify it.﴾ That is, He will obliterate it or make its falsehood manifest. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not set right the work of the corrupters.﴾ That is, He does not make it endure or strengthen it. In this is evidence that magic is corruption and deception, having no reality.

﴿And Allah will establish the truth﴾ and confirm it. ﴿by His words﴾ by His commands and decrees. It was also recited as *bi-kalimatihi* (in the singular). ﴿Even though the criminals dislike it.﴾

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 83:

﴿So none believed in Musa﴾ i.e., at the beginning of his mission. ﴿except a few offspring from among his people﴾, i.e., only some youths (awlad) from among the offspring of his people, the Children of Israel. He called them, but they did not respond to him out of fear of Fir'awn (Pharaoh), except a group of their young men. It is also said that the pronoun refers to Fir'awn, and the "offspring" (dhurriyyah) is a group of their young men who believed in him; or [the offspring are] the believer from the family of Fir'awn, his wife Asiyah, his treasurer, his wife, and his hairdresser. ﴿in fear of Fir'awn and their chiefs (mala'ihim)﴾, i.e., together with fear of them. The pronoun refers to Fir'awn, and it is in the plural in accordance with the usual usage for the pronoun of great persons; or [the pronoun refers to] his family, since the intended meaning of "Fir'awn" is his household, as one says "Rabi'ah and Mudar" (tribal names used for their collective groups); or [the pronoun refers] to "offspring" or to "people." ﴿that he would persecute them﴾, i.e., that Fir'awn would torment them. It is either a substitute (badal) for the preceding noun, or the object of "fear" (khawf). The pronoun is given in the singular to indicate that the fear of the chiefs was on account of him. ﴿Indeed, Fir'awn was haughty (la'aal) in the land﴾, i.e., dominant (laghalib) therein. ﴿And indeed he was among the extravagant (musrifin)﴾ in arrogance and tyranny, to the point that he claimed lordship and enslaved the tribes (asbat) of the prophets.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 84–86:

﴿And Moses said﴾ when he saw the fear of the believers regarding him. ﴿O my people, if you have believed in God, then rely upon Him﴾ so trust in Him and depend upon Him. ﴿if you are Muslims﴾ submitting (mustaslimin) to the decree of God, sincere (mukhlisin) toward Him. This is not a case of making the ruling conditional on two conditions (ta'liq al-hukm bi-shartayn), for what is conditioned on faith is the obligation of reliance (wujub al-tawakkul), since faith is what necessitates it (al-muqtadi lahu), while what is conditioned on Islam is its realization (husul), since it is not found together with mixing (al-takhlit). Its parallel is: "If Zayd calls you, then answer him, if you are able."

﴿So they said: In God we have put our trust﴾ because they were believers, sincere, and for this reason their supplication was answered. ﴿Our Lord, do not make us a trial﴾ (p-122) a place of trial. ﴿for the wrongdoing people﴾ meaning, do not give them power over us, so that they would subject us to trial.

﴿And save us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people﴾ from their plotting and from the evil of witnessing them. In placing reliance (tawakkul) before the supplication (du'a') there is an indication that the one who supplicates should first rely upon God so that his supplication may be answered.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 87:

﴿And We revealed to Moses and his brother: "Settle your people in Egypt in houses"﴾ — that is, take for them dwellings (maba'a). ﴿in houses for your people in Egypt, in which you dwell or to which you return for worship﴾. ﴿And make﴾ — you two and your people. ﴿your houses﴾ — those houses. ﴿a qibla﴾ — a place of prayer (musalla). It was also said: mosques facing the qibla, meaning the Ka'ba, and Moses ﷺ used to pray towards it. ﴿And establish the prayer﴾ in them. They were commanded to do this at the beginning of their affair so that the disbelievers would not gain the upper hand over them and harm them and tempt them away from their religion. ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾ of victory in this world and Paradise in the next. He used the dual pronoun at first because settling the people and taking places of worship are things undertaken by the leaders of the people through consultation; then he used the plural because making the houses mosques and praying in them is something that everyone should do; then he used the singular because giving good tidings is, in origin, the task of the bearer of the Shari'a.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 88–89:

﴿And Moses said: "Our Lord, You have indeed given Pharaoh and his chiefs adornment﴾: that by which they adorn themselves, of clothing, mounts and the like. ﴿and wealth in the life of this world﴾: kinds of property. ﴿Our Lord, so that they may lead astray from Your way﴾ is a supplication against them in the form of an imperative, given that He knew from observing their conditions that nothing else would happen, like your saying: "May God curse Iblis (Satan)." It has been said that the lam is the lam of consequence (lam al-ʿaqibah), and it is connected to ﴿You have given﴾. It may also be the lam of cause (lam al-ʿillah), because the bestowal of blessings upon disbelief is a gradual leading-on and a confirmation in error, and because, when they made them a means to error, it is as if they were given them so that they would go astray. In that case, ﴿Our Lord﴾ is a repetition of the first, for emphasis and alerting, indicating that the purpose is to present their error and ingratitude, as a preface to his saying: ﴿Our Lord, obliterate their wealth﴾, that is, destroy it. The ṭams (ṭamas) is the eradication. It was recited as (اطْمُسْ) with a ḍammah. ﴿And harden their hearts﴾, that is, make them hard and seal them, so that they do not open up to faith. ﴿So they will not believe until they see the painful punishment﴾ is the answer to the supplication, or a supplication in the form of a prohibition, or a conjunction with ﴿so that they may lead astray﴾, and what lies between them is an intervening supplication.

﴿He said: "Your supplication has been answered, you two﴾: meaning Moses and Aaron, because he used to say "Amin" (amen). ﴿So go straight﴾: remain steadfast in what you are upon of calling and establishing the proof, and do not hasten, for what you have requested will certainly occur, but in its appointed time.

It is related that he remained among them forty years after the supplication.

﴿And do not follow the way of those who do not know﴾: the path of the ignorant in haste, or in lack of certainty and assurance in God's promise, most high. It is related from Ibn ʿAmir, through the transmission of Ibn Dhakwan, that he read ﴿and do not follow﴾ with a light nun (nun al-tawkid al-khafifah) and with a kasrah on it because of the meeting of two unvocalized letters (iltiqa' al-sakinayn). ﴿And do not follow﴾ means "whoever follows." ﴿And do not follow﴾ also.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 90–91:

﴿And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea﴾. That is, We made them pass through the sea until they reached the shore, while protecting them. It is also read as «جَوَّزْنا» (*jawwaznā*), which is from the form *fa''ala* (a grammatical verb pattern, here meaning intensification), synonymous with *fā'ala*, as in *ḍa''afa* and *ḍā'afa* (both meaning "to multiply"). ﴿Then Pharaoh and his hosts pursued them﴾, that is, overtook them. It is said: "I followed him until I caught up with him." ﴿Out of wrongdoing and enmity (p-123)﴾ means transgressing and being hostile, or they are verbal nouns for transgression and enmity. It is also read as «وعُدُوًّا» (*wa-ʿudūwan*). ﴿Until, when drowning overtook him﴾, that is, reached him. ﴿He said: "I believe that﴾, that is, "that" (*annahu*). ﴿There is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am among the Muslims."﴾ Ḥamzah and al-Kisā'ī read «أنَّهُ» (*innahu*) with a kasra, on the basis of an implied verb of saying, or as a new sentence, or as an appositive and explanation of ﴿I believe﴾. ﴿Now?﴾ Do you believe now, when you have despaired of yourself and no choice remains for you? ﴿And you had disobeyed before﴾, before that, throughout the duration of your life. ﴿And you were among the corrupters﴾, the misguided and those who led others astray from faith.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 92:

﴿So today We shall save you﴾ We shall rescue you from what your people fell into, from the depths of the sea, and We shall make you float, or We shall cast you upon a high place of the earth so that the Children of Israel may see you. Ya'qub (Yaʿqub) recited (nunajjika) as man anja (from the verb anja), and it was also read as "nunhika" with a ḥāʾ, meaning We shall cast you to one side of the shore. ﴿in your body﴾ This is in the position of a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl), meaning: in your body devoid of the spirit; or whole and intact; or naked, without clothing. Or it means: in your armour, and he had a golden armour by which he was known. It was read as "bi-abdānika" (in your bodies), meaning in all the parts of the body, as in their saying "he fell with his whole body (bi-ijramihi)"; or as "bi-durū‘ika" (in your armours), as if he were wearing them over one another. ﴿so that you may be a sign for those who come after you﴾ a sign and a marker for those behind you, namely the Children of Israel, for there was in their souls of his greatness such that it was imagined to them that he would not perish, until they denied Musa, peace be upon him, when he informed them of his drowning, until they witnessed him cast up on the shore in their path. Or for those who come after you of the generations, when they hear the outcome of your affair from those who witnessed you, as a lesson and a deterrent from tyranny; or as a proof showing them that man, for all his great station and the pride of his kingship, is a subject, overpowered, far from the places of lordship. It was also read as "liman khalaqaka" (for the one who created you), meaning a sign for your Creator, like the other signs; for His singling you out for casting onto the shore is evidence that He intended it to expose your forgery and remove doubt about your affair. This indicates the perfection of His power, knowledge and will, and this interpretation is also possible according to the well-known view. ﴿And indeed, many of the people are heedless of Our signs﴾ they do not reflect upon them nor take heed from them.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 93:

﴿And We certainly settled﴾ means: We sent down. ﴿the Children of Israel in a settlement of truthfulness﴾ means: a good and pleasing dwelling place, namely al-Sham (Greater Syria) and Egypt. ﴿And We provided them with good things﴾ means: of delicious foods. ﴿And they did not differ until knowledge had come to them﴾ means: they did not differ concerning the matter of their religion except after they had read the Torah (al-Tawrah) and known its rulings; or, concerning the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ), they did not differ except after they had known his truthfulness through his attributes (as described in their scriptures) and the frequent appearance of his miracles. ﴿Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which they used to differ﴾ means: He will distinguish the one who is in the right from the one who is in the wrong, by saving and destroying.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 94–95:

﴿If you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you﴾ of the narratives, on the basis of supposition and assumption. ﴿Then ask those who have been reading the Book before you﴾ for it is established and certain among them, and firmly present in their books, in the same manner as what We have revealed to you. The purpose is to confirm that and to call upon what is in the earlier books, and that the Qur'an confirms what is in them; or it is a description of the People of the Book as firmly rooted in knowledge of the soundness of what has been sent down to you; or it is to stir up the Messenger ﷺ and to increase his steadfastness, since there is no possibility of doubt occurring to him. For this reason the Messenger ﷺ said: "I do not doubt, and I do not ask."

It has been said that the address is to the Prophet ﷺ while what is meant is his community, or to everyone who hears; that is, "If you, O listener, are in doubt about what We have sent down upon the tongue of our Prophet to you." In this there is a warning that whoever is troubled by a doubt concerning the religion should hasten to resolve it by returning to the people of knowledge. ﴿Indeed, the truth has come to you from your Lord﴾ clearly, so there is no room for doubt in it, by means of the decisive signs. ﴿So do not be among those who doubt﴾ by wavering from what you are upon of certainty and conviction.

﴿And do not be among those who denied the signs of Allah, lest you be among the losers﴾ likewise, by way of stirring up and strengthening, and cutting off any hopes concerning him, like His saying ﴿So do not be a supporter of the disbelievers﴾.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 96–97:

﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been justified﴾ — ثَبَتَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ (it has been established against them). ﴿The word of your Lord﴾ — that they will die in disbelief and be abiding in the punishment.

﴿Will not believe﴾ — because His speech is not belied and His decree is not overturned.

﴿Even if every sign should come to them﴾ — for the original cause of their faith, which is the connection of Allah the Exalted's will to them, is absent. ﴿Until they see the painful punishment﴾ — and at that time it will not benefit them, just as it did not benefit Pharaoh.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 98:

﴿Why was there not a town that believed﴾ Why was there not a town among the towns We destroyed that believed before witnessing the punishment, and did not postpone its faith as Pharaoh postponed his? ﴿So its faith benefited it﴾ by God accepting it from them and removing the punishment from them. ﴿Except the people of Yunus﴾ But the people of Yunus, peace be upon him, ﴿when they believed﴾ as soon as they saw the first signs of the punishment, and did not delay it until it descended. ﴿We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world﴾. It is also permissible for the sentence to carry the sense of negation, because the particle of urging (al-tahdid) includes that meaning. In that case the exception is contiguous (istithna' muttasil), because by "towns" is meant their inhabitants, as if he had said: no people of any sinful town believed, so that their faith benefited them, except the people of Yunus. This is supported by the reading in the nominative case (raf') as a substitute (badal). ﴿And We let them enjoy for a time﴾ until their appointed terms.

It is narrated that Yunus, peace be upon him, was sent to the people of Nineveh, of Mosul, but they denied him and persisted in their disbelief, so he promised them punishment after three days. It is said: after thirty days. It is said: after forty days. When the appointed time drew near, the sky became overcast with a black cloud containing dense smoke, and it descended until it enveloped their city. They were terrified and sought Yunus, but did not find him, so they became certain of his truthfulness. They put on woolen garments, went out to the open ground with their selves, their women, their children and their animals, and they separated every mother from her child, so that some of them longed for others, and the voices and wailing rose. They sincerely repented, showed their faith, and humbly supplicated God, the Exalted. So He had mercy on them, removed the punishment from them, and that day was the Day of Ashura, which was a Friday.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 99:

﴿And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them together.﴾ In such a way that not one of them would deviate. ﴿All of them together﴾ gathered upon faith, not differing concerning it. This is an evidence against the Qadariyya (the Qadariyya, a early school that denied divine predestination of human acts), in that He, exalted is He, did not will the faith of all of them, and that whoever He wills to have faith will certainly believe. Restricting it to a will of compulsion (mashi'at al-ilja') is contrary to the apparent meaning. ﴿Would you then compel the people﴾ with what Allah has not willed from them, ﴿until they become believers?﴾ The placing of the compulsion after the will with the particle fa' (then), and its being preceded by the interrogative particle for denial, and the placement of the pronoun before the verb, indicate that the opposite of the will is impossible, so it cannot be brought about by compulsion toward it, let alone by urging and exhortation toward it. For it is reported that he was eager for the faith of his people and very concerned with it, so this verse was revealed.

And for this reason He established it with His saying: (p-125)

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verse 100–101:

﴿And it is not for a soul to believe﴾ in Allah, ﴿except by the permission of Allah﴾, that is, except by His will, His gracious aids, and His enabling success. So do not exhaust yourself over their guidance, for it rests with Allah. ﴿And He places the defilement﴾, that is, the punishment or abandonment (al-khidhlan), for it is its cause. It is also read with a zay (ال رجز / al-rijz), and Abu Bakr read ﴿Nanjal﴾ with a nun.

﴿upon those who do not use reason﴾, that is, who do not employ their intellects in reflecting upon the proofs and signs, or who do not comprehend His indications and rulings, because of the sealing (al-taba') upon their hearts. The first interpretation is supported by His saying:

﴿Say: Look﴾, that is, reflect, ﴿at what is in the heavens and the earth﴾ of the wonders of His creation, so that they may point you to His oneness and the perfection of His power. If "what" (madha) is taken as an interrogative, it suspends (ta'liq) the verb ﴿look﴾ from taking an object. ﴿But the signs and warnings avail not a people who do not believe﴾ in the knowledge and judgment of Allah. Here "ma" is either a negation particle or an interrogative in a position of accusative (nasb).

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 102–103:

﴿Are they waiting for anything but the like of the days of those who passed away before them?﴾ That is, like their battles and the descent of God's punishment upon them, since they deserve nothing other than that. This is from their saying "the days of the Arabs" (ayyam al-'Arab) for their battles.

﴿Say: Then wait; I am with you among those who wait.﴾ That is, wait for that (the punishment), or: wait for my destruction, "I am with you among those who wait" for your destruction.

﴿Then We deliver Our messengers and those who believe.﴾ It is coordinated (ʿutifa) with an omitted element indicated by ﴿but the like of the days of those who passed away﴾. It is as if it were said: We destroy the nations, then We deliver Our messengers and those who believe in them, in narration of the past circumstance. ﴿Thus it is an obligation upon Us that We deliver the believers.﴾ "Thus" refers to the deliverance: that is, deliverance of this kind, or a deliverance like this; We deliver Muhammad and his companions when We destroy the polytheists. The phrase ﴿an obligation upon Us﴾ is a parenthetical insertion (i'tiraD), and its accusative is governed by a verb understood. It is also said that it is a substitute (badal) for "thus." Hafs and al-Kisa'i read (nunjī) with a light (mukhaffaf) pronunciation.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 104–105:

﴿Say: O mankind,﴾ an address to the people of Makkah. ﴿If you are in doubt about my religion﴾ and its soundness. ﴿then I do not worship those whom you worship besides Allah, but I worship Allah, who causes you to die.﴾ This is the summary of my religion, in belief and in practice. Present it to pure reason and look at it with an eye of fairness, so that you may know its soundness, which is this: I do not worship what you create and worship, but I worship your Creator, who brings you into being and causes you to die. The mention of causing to die was singled out for the sake of warning (tahdid). ﴿And I am commanded to be among the believers﴾ in what reason indicates and revelation speaks of. The omission of the preposition before an-anna (ʾan, "that") is permissible; it is among the regular cases with ʾan and in other cases too, as in his saying:

A poet's verse:
"I commanded you to good, so do what you were commanded, for I have left you possessing wealth and lineage."

﴿And that I should set your face toward the religion﴾ is coordinated with ﴿that I should be﴾, except that the relative clause of ʾan is expressed in the imperative form, and there is no difference between them in purpose, because the intent is to connect it to what contains the meaning of the verbal noun (maṣdar), so that it indicates that meaning together with it. All verb forms are like this, whether the declarative or the imperative. The meaning is: I am commanded to be upright in the religion and to be steadfast in it by performing the obligations and refraining from vile deeds, or, regarding prayer, by facing the qibla. ﴿Ḥanīfan﴾ is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from "the religion" or from "the face". ﴿And do not be among the polytheists.﴾

﴿And if Allah touches you with harm﴾ — that is, if He afflicts you with it. ﴿None can remove it﴾ — none can lift it. ﴿except Him﴾ — except Allah. ﴿And if He intends for you good﴾ — that is, He wills it for you, ﴿none can repel His bounty﴾ — none can ward off His favour by which He intends you. Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 10, verses 108–109:

﴿Say: "O mankind, the truth has certainly come to you from your Lord"﴾ — that is, His Messenger or the Qur'an — "and there remains for you no excuse." ﴿So whoever is guided﴾ by faith and following, ﴿it is only for himself that he is guided﴾, because its benefit returns to him. ﴿And whoever goes astray﴾ by disbelief in both of them, ﴿it is only against himself that he goes astray﴾, because the burden of straying falls upon him. ﴿And I am not over you a guardian﴾ — that is, a keeper entrusted with your affairs — "and I am only a bringer of good news and a warner."

﴿And follow what is revealed to you﴾ by complying and conveying it. ﴿And be patient﴾ over their call and bear their harm. ﴿Until Allah judges﴾ — by granting victory or by ordering fighting. ﴿And He is the best of judges﴾, since error is impossible in His judgment, for His knowledge of inner secrets is like His knowledge of outward appearances.

From the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surah Yunus will be given the reward of ten good deeds for every person who believed in Yunus and denied him, and for every person who drowned with Pharaoh."
